claim: Rspo3 is expressed in bone during mouse skeletal development.
source: Rspo3 is expressed in bone during mouse skeletal development (Nam et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nam et al., 2007

claim: Rspo3 expression increases significantly during osteoblast differentiation in primary calvarial osteoblasts.
source: We assessed Rspo3 mRNA levels in primary calvarial osteoblasts (cOBs) and found that it is expressed in these cells and that its expression increases significantly during OB differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a

claim: Global deletion of Rspo3 leads to lethality by E9.5 in mice.
source: As global deletion of Rspo3 leads to lethality by E9.5 (Aoki et al., 2007; Kazanskaya et al., 2008), before skeletal development, we analyzed mice lacking only one Rspo3 allele (Rspo3+/-) and their WT littermates.
evidence: Supported by citations to Aoki et al., 2007 and Kazanskaya et al., 2008

claim: Rspo3+/- mice are born at the expected Mendelian ratio.
source: Rspo3+/- mice are born at the expected Mendelian ratio and their axial and appendicular skeleton develop normally (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation and Figure 1—figure supplement 1b

claim: The axial and appendicular skeleton develop normally in Rspo3+/- mice.
source: Rspo3+/- mice are born at the expected Mendelian ratio and their axial and appendicular skeleton develop normally (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation and Figure 1—figure supplement 1b

claim: Rspo3+/- mice remain healthy and do not develop any detectable pathology as they age up to one year.
source: Rspo3+/- mice continue to be healthy and do not develop any detectable pathology as they age (up to one year) (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation over time

claim: Rspo3 mRNA levels are significantly decreased by 50% in Rspo3+/- mice compared with WT mice in marrow-depleted long bones.
source: We confirmed that Rspo3 mRNA levels were significantly decreased (50%) in Rspo3+/- mice in both marrow-depleted long bones and in cultured cOBs compared with WT mice (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency has highly significant anabolic effects on skeletal parameters in both female and male mice at 6, 12, and 18 weeks of age.
source: Contrary to expectations, two-way ANOVA analysis of the skeletal phenotype at 6, 12, and 18 wk of age (Figure 1b, Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Supplementary file 1), revealed highly significant (P<0.001) anabolic effects of Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency on structural, cellular, and dynamic parameters in both female and male mice.
evidence: Supported by two-way ANOVA analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1b, Table 1, and supplementary files

claim: Rspo3+/- mice exhibit increased trabecular bone mass with high bone formation, mineral apposition rate and osteoblast number and surface.
source: The skeletal phenotype of Rspo3+/- male and female mice is overall characterized by an increase in trabecular bone mass with high bone formation, mineral apposition rate and OB number and surface whereas bone resorption parameters are not affected, as indicated by osteoclast (OC) number and surface as well as eroded surface (ES/BS) (Figure 1b, Table 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b, Table 1, and Supplementary file 1

claim: Bone resorption parameters are not affected in Rspo3+/- mice.
source: The skeletal phenotype of Rspo3+/- male and female mice is overall characterized by an increase in trabecular bone mass with high bone formation, mineral apposition rate and OB number and surface whereas bone resorption parameters are not affected, as indicated by osteoclast (OC) number and surface as well as eroded surface (ES/BS) (Figure 1b, Table 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no changes in osteoclast parameters

claim: At 12 weeks of age, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency leads to a significant increase in trabecular bone mass (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th.), and trabecular number (Tb.N).
source: At 12 wk of age Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a significant increase in trabecular bone mass (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th.), and trabecular number (Tb.N) (Figure 1c–d, Table 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c-d, Table 1, and Supplementary file 1

claim: Trabecular bone resorption parameters (Oc.S/B.Pm and N.Oc/B.Pm) were not changed in both Rspo3+/- male and female mice at 12 weeks of age.
source: Trabecular bone resorption parameters (Oc.S/B.Pm and N.Oc/B.Pm) were not changed in both Rspo3+/- male and female mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no changes in osteoclast parameters

claim: Rspo3+/- mice exhibited an increase in trabecular bone formation parameters (BFR/BS).
source: In contrast, Rspo3+/- mice exhibited an increase in trabecular bone formation parameters (BFR/BS) (Figure 1d–e, Table 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d-e, Table 1, and Supplementary file 1

claim: The increase in BFR in Rspo3+/- mice is associated with an increase in mineral apposition rate (MAR).
source: This increase in BFR was associated with an increase in mineral apposition rate (MAR), indicating a marked increase in the activity of individual OBs in Rspo3+/- mice, in addition to the increase in their numbers (N.Ob/B.pm, Figure 1d, Table 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased MAR in Rspo3+/- mice

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency indicates a marked increase in the activity of individual osteoblasts.
source: This increase in BFR was associated with an increase in mineral apposition rate (MAR), indicating a marked increase in the activity of individual OBs in Rspo3+/- mice, in addition to the increase in their numbers (N.Ob/B.pm, Figure 1d, Table 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Inferred from increased MAR and BFR data

claim: The osteoid surface (OS/BS) and the osteoblast surface (Ob.S/B.Pm) were significantly increased in both sexes of Rspo3+/- mice.
source: Consistent with these results, the osteoid surface (OS/BS) and the OB surface (Ob.S/B.Pm) were also significantly increased in both sexes (Table 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 1

claim: Cortical bone parameters were not significantly changed in Rspo3+/- female and male mice at 12 weeks of age.
source: Despite these marked effects on trabecular bone, cortical bone parameters were not significantly changed in Rspo3+/- female and male mice at 12 wk of age (Figure 1d, Supplementary file 2 and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d and supplementary files

claim: No significant differences in bone mass or cellular activities were noted in the vertebrae (L5) of Rspo3+/- mice at 12 weeks of age.
source: In contrast to the observed effects in the tibia, no significant differences in bone mass or cellular activities were noted in the vertebrae (L5) at 12 wk of age (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 4), indicating that Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency affects preferentially the trabecular bone compartment in long bones.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 4

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency affects preferentially the trabecular bone compartment in long bones.
source: In contrast to the observed effects in the tibia, no significant differences in bone mass or cellular activities were noted in the vertebrae (L5) at 12 wk of age (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 4), indicating that Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency affects preferentially the trabecular bone compartment in long bones.
evidence: Inferred from differential effects in tibia versus vertebrae

claim: Rspo3 is expressed in bone marrow macrophage (BMM)-derived osteoclasts.
source: In agreement with our in vivo observations, we found that, although Rspo3 is expressed in bone marrow macrophage (BMM)-derived OCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), there were no significant differences in the formation of TRAP+ multinucleated cells and in the expression of OC marker genes (Ctsk, Trap, Nfatc1) between BMM cultures from WT and Rspo3+/- in response to M-CSF and RANKL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b and c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a

claim: There were no significant differences in the formation of TRAP+ multinucleated cells between BMM cultures from WT and Rspo3+/- mice in response to M-CSF and RANKL.
source: In agreement with our in vivo observations, we found that, although Rspo3 is expressed in bone marrow macrophage (BMM)-derived OCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), there were no significant differences in the formation of TRAP+ multinucleated cells and in the expression of OC marker genes (Ctsk, Trap, Nfatc1) between BMM cultures from WT and Rspo3+/- in response to M-CSF and RANKL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b and c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b and c

claim: There were no significant differences in the expression of osteoclast marker genes (Ctsk, Trap, Nfatc1) between BMM cultures from WT and Rspo3+/- mice.
source: In agreement with our in vivo observations, we found that, although Rspo3 is expressed in bone marrow macrophage (BMM)-derived OCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), there were no significant differences in the formation of TRAP+ multinucleated cells and in the expression of OC marker genes (Ctsk, Trap, Nfatc1) between BMM cultures from WT and Rspo3+/- in response to M-CSF and RANKL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b and c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3c

claim: Mix-and-matched co-cultures of calvarial osteoblasts and BMMs from WT or Rspo3+/- mice confirmed that Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency does not affect osteoclastogenesis, whether directly or indirectly.
source: In addition, mix-and-matched co-cultures of cOBs and BMMs from WT or Rspo3+/- mice confirmed that Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency does not affect osteoclastogenesis, whether directly or indirectly (Figure 1—figure supplement 3d).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3d

claim: The total number of bone stromal cells (Lin-CD45-) was not significantly affected by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency.
source: Bone marrow flow cytometry showed that while the total number of bone stromal cells (Lin-CD45-) was not significantly affected by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency (4047±1245 in WT compared with 5867+2382 in Rspo3+/-, mean ± SEM n=10), the mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) population (defined here as Lin-CD45-CD31-CD51+Sca-1+) (Schepers et al., 2013) was significantly increased in Rspo3+/- mice compared with WT littermates (p=0.015) (Figure 2a and b).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data

claim: The mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) population (Lin-CD45-CD31-CD51+Sca-1+) was significantly increased in Rspo3+/- mice compared with WT littermates.
source: Bone marrow flow cytometry showed that while the total number of bone stromal cells (Lin-CD45-) was not significantly affected by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency (4047±1245 in WT compared with 5867+2382 in Rspo3+/-, mean ± SEM n=10), the mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) population (defined here as Lin-CD45-CD31-CD51+Sca-1+) (Schepers et al., 2013) was significantly increased in Rspo3+/- mice compared with WT littermates (p=0.015) (Figure 2a and b).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2a and b with p=0.015

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency significantly increased CFU-F formation.
source: Consistent with these findings and with the observed increase in OB number and bone formation, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency significantly increased CFU-F (p=0.04), and CFU-OB (p=0.034) formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c with p=0.04

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency significantly increased CFU-OB formation.
source: Consistent with these findings and with the observed increase in OB number and bone formation, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency significantly increased CFU-F (p=0.04), and CFU-OB (p=0.034) formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c with p=0.034

claim: Treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-F potential of WT BMSCs.
source: Importantly, while treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-F and CFU-OB potential of WT BMSCs, it showed a tendency to decrease CFU-F and rescued significantly, i.e., prevented, the Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency-dependent increase in CFU-OB formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c

claim: Treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-OB potential of WT BMSCs.
source: Importantly, while treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-F and CFU-OB potential of WT BMSCs, it showed a tendency to decrease CFU-F and rescued significantly, i.e., prevented, the Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency-dependent increase in CFU-OB formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c

claim: Treatment with recombinant Rspo3 showed a tendency to decrease CFU-F in Rspo3+/- BMSCs.
source: Importantly, while treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-F and CFU-OB potential of WT BMSCs, it showed a tendency to decrease CFU-F and rescued significantly, i.e., prevented, the Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency-dependent increase in CFU-OB formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c

claim: Treatment with recombinant Rspo3 rescued significantly the Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency-dependent increase in CFU-OB formation.
source: Importantly, while treatment with recombinant Rspo3 did not affect the CFU-F and CFU-OB potential of WT BMSCs, it showed a tendency to decrease CFU-F and rescued significantly, i.e., prevented, the Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency-dependent increase in CFU-OB formation (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c

claim: The changes induced by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency cell-autonomously affect the bone marrow MSC lineage.
source: These data show that the changes induced by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency cell-autonomously affect the bone marrow MSC lineage and induce an increase in the pool of progenitor cells with OB potential.
evidence: Inferred from CFU and flow cytometry data showing increased MSC and osteoblast progenitors

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency induces an increase in the pool of progenitor cells with osteoblast potential.
source: These data show that the changes induced by Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency cell-autonomously affect the bone marrow MSC lineage and induce an increase in the pool of progenitor cells with OB potential.
evidence: Supported by CFU-OB and MSC population data

claim: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Rspo3-OB-cKO) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice.
source: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Figure 3a) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice as indicated by a significant increase in BV/TV (females p=0.017, males p<0.0001), MAR (females p=0.0034, males p<0.0001), BFR/BS (females p=0.0012, males p<0.0001) and N.Ob/B.Pm (p=0.033, males p=0.007) in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) littermates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing similar phenotypes in Rspo3-OB-cKO and Rspo3+/- mice

claim: Rspo3-OB-cKO mice showed a significant increase in BV/TV compared with control littermates.
source: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Figure 3a) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice as indicated by a significant increase in BV/TV (females p=0.017, males p<0.0001), MAR (females p=0.0034, males p<0.0001), BFR/BS (females p=0.0012, males p<0.0001) and N.Ob/B.Pm (p=0.033, males p=0.007) in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) littermates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data with p-values

claim: Rspo3-OB-cKO mice showed a significant increase in MAR compared with control littermates.
source: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Figure 3a) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice as indicated by a significant increase in BV/TV (females p=0.017, males p<0.0001), MAR (females p=0.0034, males p<0.0001), BFR/BS (females p=0.0012, males p<0.0001) and N.Ob/B.Pm (p=0.033, males p=0.007) in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) littermates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data with p-values

claim: Rspo3-OB-cKO mice showed a significant increase in BFR/BS compared with control littermates.
source: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Figure 3a) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice as indicated by a significant increase in BV/TV (females p=0.017, males p<0.0001), MAR (females p=0.0034, males p<0.0001), BFR/BS (females p=0.0012, males p<0.0001) and N.Ob/B.Pm (p=0.033, males p=0.007) in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) littermates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data with p-values

claim: Rspo3-OB-cKO mice showed a significant increase in N.Ob/B.Pm compared with control littermates.
source: OB lineage-targeted deletion of Rspo3 (Figure 3a) reproduced the skeletal phenotype seen in the appendicular skeleton of Rspo3+/- mice as indicated by a significant increase in BV/TV (females p=0.017, males p<0.0001), MAR (females p=0.0034, males p<0.0001), BFR/BS (females p=0.0012, males p<0.0001) and N.Ob/B.Pm (p=0.033, males p=0.007) in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) littermates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data with p-values

claim: There were no changes in osteoclast parameters in Rspo3-OB-cKO mice.
source: Once again there were no changes in OC parameters (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Supplementary file 5

claim: μCT analysis of the femur confirmed a significant increase in BV/TV, Tb.N, and Conn.D in both males and females of Rspo3-OB-cKO mice.
source: μCT analysis of the femur, confirmed a significant increase in BV/TV, Tb.N, and Conn.D in both males and females (Figure 3d).
evidence: Supported by μCT data shown in Figure 3d

claim: The basal expression level of Rspo3 and the efficiency of deletion in long bones and vertebrae were similar.
source: Very surprisingly, however, and although the basal expression level of Rspo3 and the efficiency of deletion in long bones and vertebrae were similar (Figure 3a and Figure 4a), L5 μCT analysis showed a significant decrease in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, and Conn.D accompanied by a marked increase in Tb.Sp. and SMI in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) male and female littermates (Figure 4b), confirming a recent report (Nilsson et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a and Figure 4a

claim: L5 μCT analysis showed a significant decrease in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, and Conn.D in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with control littermates.
source: Very surprisingly, however, and although the basal expression level of Rspo3 and the efficiency of deletion in long bones and vertebrae were similar (Figure 3a and Figure 4a), L5 μCT analysis showed a significant decrease in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, and Conn.D accompanied by a marked increase in Tb.Sp. and SMI in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) male and female littermates (Figure 4b), confirming a recent report (Nilsson et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by μCT data shown in Figure 4b

claim: L5 μCT analysis showed a marked increase in Tb.Sp. and SMI in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with control littermates.
source: Very surprisingly, however, and although the basal expression level of Rspo3 and the efficiency of deletion in long bones and vertebrae were similar (Figure 3a and Figure 4a), L5 μCT analysis showed a significant decrease in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, and Conn.D accompanied by a marked increase in Tb.Sp. and SMI in Rspo3-OB-cKO compared with their control (Rspo3fl) male and female littermates (Figure 4b), confirming a recent report (Nilsson et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by μCT data shown in Figure 4b

claim: Bone histomorphometry analysis showed that structural parameters were significantly decreased in Rspo3-OB-cKO males compared with the control group.
source: Bone histomorphometry analysis showed that structural parameters were also significantly decreased but only in Rspo3-OB-cKO males compared with the control group (Figure 4c–d and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: Supported by histomorphometry data shown in Figure 4c-d and Supplementary file 6

claim: No significant changes were seen in the dynamic parameters in vertebrae of Rspo3-OB-cKO mice.
source: No significant changes were seen in the dynamic parameters.
evidence: Supported by histomorphometry data

claim: The N.Ob/B.Pm and Ob.S/BS were not changed in vertebrae of Rspo3-OB-cKO mice.
source: While the N.Ob/B.Pm and Ob.S/BS were not changed, the N.Oc/ B.Pm was significantly increased in Rspo3-OB-cKO males but not females, compared with the control group (Figure 4d and Supplementary file 6), providing a possible explanation for the decreased bone mass, at least in males.
evidence: Supported by histomorphometry data shown in Figure 4d and Supplementary file 6

claim: The N.Oc/B.Pm was significantly increased in Rspo3-OB-cKO males but not females, compared with the control group.
source: While the N.Ob/B.Pm and Ob.S/BS were not changed, the N.Oc/ B.Pm was significantly increased in Rspo3-OB-cKO males but not females, compared with the control group (Figure 4d and Supplementary file 6), providing a possible explanation for the decreased bone mass, at least in males.
evidence: Supported by histomorphometry data shown in Figure 4d and Supplementary file 6

claim: Targeted deletion of Rspo3 in Runx2+ osteoprogenitors leads to an opposite bone phenotype in the appendicular and the axial skeleton.
source: Thus, our studies show that targeted deletion of Rspo3 in Runx2+ osteoprogenitors leads to an opposite bone phenotype in the appendicular and the axial skeleton.
evidence: Inferred from the contrasting effects in long bones versus vertebrae

claim: μCT analysis of the femur and L5 vertebrae did not show any structural difference in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, or Tb.Sp between Runx2-Cre, WT, and Rspo3fl mice.
source: Excluding any effect of the transgene or the floxed allele on the differential effect of Rspo3 targeted deletion in the axial and appendicular skeleton, μCT analysis of the femur and L5 vertebrae did not show any structural difference in BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, or Tb.Sp between Runx2-Cre, WT, and Rspo3fl mice (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by μCT data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a remarkable increase in the expression of canonical Wnt target genes Axin2 and Tcf7 in BMSCs.
source: Surprisingly, but consistent with our observations on bone formation, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a remarkable increase in the expression of known canonical Wnt target genes Axin2 and Tcf7 and increased active β-catenin levels (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5a

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency increased active β-catenin levels in BMSCs.
source: Surprisingly, but consistent with our observations on bone formation, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a remarkable increase in the expression of known canonical Wnt target genes Axin2 and Tcf7 and increased active β-catenin levels (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5b

claim: Runx2 expression was significantly increased in Rspo3+/- BMSCs.
source: In addition, Runx2 expression was also significantly increased in Rspo3+/- BMSCs (Figure 5a).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5a

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a significant increase in the expression of Axin2 and Dkk1 in marrow depleted long bone cortical bone.
source: In addition, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a significant increase in the expression of Axin2 and Dkk1, but not Sost in marrow depleted long bone cortical bone (Figure 5c).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5c

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency did not affect Sost expression in marrow depleted long bone cortical bone.
source: In addition, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency led to a significant increase in the expression of Axin2 and Dkk1, but not Sost in marrow depleted long bone cortical bone (Figure 5c).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5c

claim: Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency leads to activation of canonical Wnt signaling.
source: Thus, surprisingly but consistent with the bone and OB phenotypes, Rspo3 haplo-insufficiency leads to activation of canonical Wnt signaling.
evidence: Inferred from increased expression of Wnt target genes and increased β-catenin levels

claim: Rspo3 does not activate Wnt signaling by itself in WT MEFs.
source: As shown by several groups (de Lau et al., 2014; de Lau et al., 2012; Raslan and Yoon, 2019; Park et al., 2018), we confirmed that while Rspo3 does not activate Wnt signaling by itself, it potentiates exogenous Wnt3a action in WT MEFs as indicated by the Tcf7/Lef luciferase reporter assay (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data and citations

claim: Rspo3 potentiates exogenous Wnt3a action in WT MEFs.
source: As shown by several groups (de Lau et al., 2014; de Lau et al., 2012; Raslan and Yoon, 2019; Park et al., 2018), we confirmed that while Rspo3 does not activate Wnt signaling by itself, it potentiates exogenous Wnt3a action in WT MEFs as indicated by the Tcf7/Lef luciferase reporter assay (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a and citations

claim: At steady-state, Rspo3 deficiency led to a marked increase in the expression of the canonical Wnt target genes Tcf7 and Axin2 in MEFs.
source: However, similar to what is observed in Rspo3 haplo-insufficient BMSCs and bone marrow depleted long bones cortical bone, at steady-state Rspo3 deficiency (p<0.0001) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) led to a marked increase in the expression of the canonical Wnt target genes Tcf7 (p<0.0001) and Axin2 (p=0.0017) as well as to a significant increase in the levels of phorphorylated Lrp6 (pLrp6), activated β-catenin and Tcf1 (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by gene expression and Western blot data shown in Figure 6a and b

claim: At steady-state, Rspo3 deficiency led to a significant increase in the levels of phosphorylated Lrp6 (pLrp6), activated β-catenin and Tcf1 in MEFs.
source: However, similar to what is observed in Rspo3 haplo-insufficient BMSCs and bone marrow depleted long bones cortical bone, at steady-state Rspo3 deficiency (p<0.0001) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) led to a marked increase in the expression of the canonical Wnt target genes Tcf7 (p<0.0001) and Axin2 (p=0.0017) as well as to a significant increase in the levels of phorphorylated Lrp6 (pLrp6), activated β-catenin and Tcf1 (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6b

claim: At steady state, TOPflash reporter activity was significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs compared with WT MEFs.
source: Accordingly, at steady state TOPflash reporter activity was significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs compared with WT MEFs (Figure 6a).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 6a

claim: Upon Wnt3a treatment, Axin2 and Tcf7 gene expression were increased in WT MEFs but were significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs.
source: Upon Wnt3a treatment, as expected, Axin2, and Tcf7 gene expression as well as pLrp6, activated β-catenin levels and TOPflash reporter activity were increased in WT MEFs but were significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by gene expression and reporter assay data shown in Figure 6a and b

claim: Upon Wnt3a treatment, pLrp6 and activated β-catenin levels were increased in WT MEFs but were significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs.
source: Upon Wnt3a treatment, as expected, Axin2, and Tcf7 gene expression as well as pLrp6, activated β-catenin levels and TOPflash reporter activity were increased in WT MEFs but were significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6b

claim: Upon Wnt3a treatment, TOPflash reporter activity was increased in WT MEFs but was significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs.
source: Upon Wnt3a treatment, as expected, Axin2, and Tcf7 gene expression as well as pLrp6, activated β-catenin levels and TOPflash reporter activity were increased in WT MEFs but were significantly higher in Rspo3 null MEFs (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 6a

claim: Haplo-insufficiency and absence of Rspo3 in BMSCs and MEFs led to β-catenin stabilization and enhancement of β-catenin-dependent signaling.
source: Thus, haplo-insufficiency and absence of Rspo3 in BMSCs and MEFs led to β-catenin stabilization and enhancement of β-catenin-dependent signaling.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental data showing increased β-catenin levels and Wnt target gene expression

claim: Wnt3a significantly decreased the expression of Rspo3 in WT MEFs.
source: Interestingly, we found that Wnt3a significantly decreased the expression of Rspo3 in WT MEFs, whereas it is significantly increased by Dkk1 (Figure 7a).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 7a

claim: Dkk1 significantly increased the expression of Rspo3 in WT MEFs.
source: Interestingly, we found that Wnt3a significantly decreased the expression of Rspo3 in WT MEFs, whereas it is significantly increased by Dkk1 (Figure 7a).

claim: Rspo3 has a dual mode of action to regulate canonical Wnt signaling and bone formation based on the regulation of two distinct signaling cascades and their crosstalk.
source: Based on our observations, we propose that Rspo3 has a dual mode of action to regulate canonical Wnt signaling and bone formation. This duality is based on the regulation of two distinct signaling cascades and their crosstalk: Rspo3 functions via both the Lgr/Rnf43/Znrf3 and the Lgr/Erk axes, and while activation of the Lgr/Rnf43/Znrf3 axis boosts Wnt signaling strength by the membrane clearance of Rnf43/Znrf3 and subsequent stabilization of Fzd receptors, binding of Rspo3 to Lgr impairs Erk signaling, preventing Erk signaling activation and further stabilization of β−catenin (Figure 10).
evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental data and proposed as a model
